pattern_name: Present perfect for experience (ever / never, been)
formula: Subject + have/has + past participle · ever (?) · never (−) · been to
when_to_use: Talk about life experiences without saying WHEN: have/has + past participle; ever in questions, never in negatives.
when_to_use_ar: للكلام عن خبرات الحياة بدون تحديد الوقت: have/has + التصريف الثالث؛ ever في السؤال، never في النفي.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: The present perfect has no direct Arabic equivalent, so learners use the past simple ('Did you ever go…?') and confuse 'been' (visited and returned) with 'gone' (went and still there).

examples.en: Have you ever been to London?
examples.ar: هل سبق أن ذهبت إلى لندن؟

examples.en: She has been to three countries.

common_errors.wrong: She has gone to Cairo. (and is back)

quick_rule: Experience (no time) → have/has + past participle. ever (?), never (−), been (there & back).
quick_rule_ar: خبرة بدون وقت → have/has + التصريف الثالث. ever للسؤال، never للنفي، been (راح ورجع).
mnemonic: Life experience, no 'when' → HAVE + past participle.
connect_to_speaking: Ask a partner: 'Have you ever travelled abroad?' 'Yes, I've been to two countries, but I've never flown alone.'
